Study finds slightly higher risk of autism diagnosis in areas with more lithium in drinking water, but experts say more research is needed

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 5 min read (986 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A newly introduced study found a moderately higher risk of autism spectrum disorder in children born to pregnant people exposed to tap water with higher levels of lithium, but experts caution that this association does not show a direct link between the two.
  • About 1 in 36 children in the US is diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) each year, according to data from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
  • Scientists still don’t know the exact cause of autism, a developmental disorder.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly introduced study found a moderately higher risk of autism spectrum disorder in children born to pregnant people exposed to tap water with higher levels of lithium, but experts caution that this association does not show a direct link between the two.

About 1 in 36 children in the US is diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) each year, according to data from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Scientists still don’t know the exact cause of autism, a developmental disorder. Genetics may be a factor, but some have been looking at potential environmental causes, too.

Autism diagnosis has become more common, but pandemic disrupted early detection, CDC indicates.

Industry observers note that cases may be on the rise, but that is also unclear. One study published this year on cases in the Latest York-New Jersey area found that autism diagnosis rates tripled among certain age groups between 2000 and 2016. A 2021 report found similar increases in cases, but the CDC says the increased number of cases is most likely linked to more doctors screening for the condition.

Lithium is an alkali metal that can be found naturally in some food and ground water. It’s used in batteries, grease and air conditioners, as well as in the treatment of bipolar disorder and some blood disorders. Its levels in US drinking water are not regulated, according to the US Geological Survey.

A new study, published Monday in the journal JAMA Pediatrics, found a small association between lithium and autism diagnosis in Denmark, where the researchers say the level of lithium in drinking water is similar to that in American water systems.

Recent findings suggest that the researchers checked a database of people with psychiatric disorders for children born between 2000 and 2013 to find information on 8,842 cases of ASD and 43,864 participants who did not have ASD. They then measured the concentration of lithium in 151 public waterworks that served more than half of the Danish population and mapped out where pregnant people lived in relation.

For many neurodiverse people, 'The Sims' has been a lifelong comfort.

According to recent reports, as lithium levels in water increased, there was a modest increased risk of an ASD diagnosis. Specifically, compared with people at the lowest exposure level, those who had the second and third highest exposure during pregnancy had a 24% to 26% higher risk of ASD diagnosed in children. The group with the highest exposure had a 46% higher risk than those at the lowest level of exposure.

The researchers could not tell how much water the pregnant people drank, but they picked Denmark in part because residents there consume some of the lowest amounts of bottled water in Europe.

Experts say it’s important to note that the research can’t show that lithium exposure leads directly to an autism diagnosis.

Further study is required, said study co-author Dr. Beate Ritz, a professor of neurology in the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA, and a professor of epidemiology and environmental health at the UCLA Fielding School of Public Health.

Industry observers note that “Any drinking water contaminants that may affect the developing human brain deserve intense scrutiny,” Ritz stated in a news release. She added that the research would need to be replicated in other countries to look for a similar connection.

Industry observers note that the implications of the findings are complex as far as public health policy is concerned, according to an editorial published alongside the study. Lithium levels in water, at concentrations that the study associated with a potential ASD risk, have also been linked with health benefits such as lower rates of hospitalization for psychiatric disorders and suicide.

“If all these of associations are valid, the wisdom of Solomon will be required to develop guidelines for lithium in drinking water that are maximally protective of the entire population,” wrote Dr. David C. Bellinger, a professor of neurology and psychology at Harvard Medical School. “Until the basic biology of ASD is better understood, it will be difficult to distinguish causal from spurious associations.”.

'Heartbreaking' delays in autism diagnosis and treatment got even worse during pandemic.

Dr. Max Wiznitzer, director of the Rainbow Autism Center at University Hospitals Rainbow Babies and Children’s Hospital in Cleveland, points to other research on the effects of lithium on pregnant people who take it for mental health disorders. Those studies – which look at people exposed to much higher levels than are found in drinking water – do not show a connection with autism spectrum disorder.

According to recent reports, “It’s an interesting association, but causation is definitely not proven,” mentioned Wiznitzer, who was not involved in the newly introduced research. “We have to see if there’s a viable and biologically plausible mechanism by which a small amount of lithium in the water supply can somehow do this, yet pharmacologic dosing of lithium in women with bipolar disorder has not been reported to be causing increased risk of ASD.”.

Other studies have also suggested connections between ASD and environmental exposures to things like pesticides, air pollution and phthalates. But none of them points to any of these factors as a direct cause of the disorder.

Industry observers note that A link between environmental exposure and ASD is hard to prove, Wiznitzer stated. With research showing that increased exposure to air pollution raises the risk of giving birth to a child with ASD, for example, he often wonders whether pollution is the determining factor or if it’s just the populations who live in more polluted areas.

“There’s a lot of speculation about about environmental factors, but how many of them are truly causally associated?” Wiznitzer said. “We are bombarded with a variety of environmental stressors in our everyday lives. We have to figure out how to basically safely navigate them, and this is probably not one that’s high on our list.”.

Syrian refugee elected mayor of German town, years after fleeing war

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Syrian who arrived in Germany as a refugee in 2015 has won a mayoral election in the southwestern German state of Baden-Württemberg.
  • Ryyan Alshebl, who left his hometown of As Suwayda in Syria eight years ago, ran as an independent in the municipality of Ostelsheim.
  • Locals cheered the 29-year-old when he welcomed his win, a victory he described as “sensational,” German local broadcaster SWR reported Monday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Syrian who arrived in Germany as a refugee in 2015 has won a mayoral election in the southwestern German state of Baden-Württemberg.

Ryyan Alshebl, who left his hometown of As Suwayda in Syria eight years ago, ran as an independent in the municipality of Ostelsheim. He won 55.41% of the votes on Sunday, beating two German candidates, Marco Strauss and Mathias Fey.

Locals cheered the 29-year-old when he welcomed his win, a victory he described as “sensational,” German local broadcaster SWR reported Monday.

“Today, Ostelsheim sent an example for broad-mindedness and cosmopolitanism for the whole of Germany,” he stated, according to to German public broadcaster ZDF. “That’s not something that can be taken for granted in a conservative, rural area.”.

Alshebl’s first call after his victory was to his mother in Syria, who was thrilled with the news, SWR reported.

Recent findings suggest that the Association of Municipalities of Baden-Württemberg noted Alshebl is the first man with Syrian roots to run for and win a mayor’s office. He will start his role in June.

'You are not a refugee.' Roma refugees fleeing war in Ukraine say they are suffering discrimination and prejudice.

According to recent reports, ostelsheim residents have welcomed their incoming mayor. “The fairy tale has come true, and the right man has become our mayor,” Annette Keck, who lives in the village, told SWR.

Sources indicate that strauss, one of his opponents, congratulated Alshebl. “I wish you good luck and at the same time ask for support for Mr. Alshebl, for our shared Ostelsheim,” he said on Facebook.

The state’s Integration Minister Manne Lucha mentioned that Alshebl’s victory showed that diversity is a natural part of Baden-Württemberg. “I would be very pleased if Ryyan Alshebl’s election encourages more people with a migration history to run for political office,” he said.

It has been revealed that not everyone has been so warm to the 29-year-old. ZDF reported the Syrian received hateful comments on the campaign trail.

The young politician went from house to house, promoting his election program, and “the experiences were predominantly positive,” but there was also a minority of far-right fringe voters in Ostelsheim that did not want to accept him due to his Syrian roots, Alshebl told ZDF.

Born to a schoolteacher and agricultural engineer in Syria, Alshebl described his life as carefree until the age of 20, according to his campaign website.

Industry observers note that at the time, protests against the Syrian government that began in 2011 soon devolved into chaotic war. The fighting and later rise of ISIS forced 10.6 million people from home by late 2015 – about half of Syria’s pre-war population.

Alshebl faced the dilemma of being drafted for military service with the Syrian army or leaving the country, according to his website.

While many Syrians were displaced internally or fled to countries in the region, others like Alshebl made the dangerous journey to Europe. He was 21 years old at the time, and said he crossed from Turkey to the Greek island of Lesbos in a rubber dinghy.

Former German Chancellor Angela Merkel had implemented a brief open-door policy in 2015 that saw the country take in about 1.2 million asylum seekers in the following years, including Alshebl.

Industry observers note that they were welcomed into British homes. Celebrating their first Christmas together, Ukrainians wonder if that hospitality will last.

The move sparked a backlash in Germany and the sudden growth of the far-right, anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the wake of summer 2015.

Once in Germany, Alshebl lived close to Ostelsheim and said at the time he felt “there is only one thing you can do: get back on your feet swiftly and start investing in your own future quickly.”.

For the last seven years he worked in the administration of Althengstett town hall, in a neighboring town. He drew from his experience, he stated in his campaign, and made digital access to to public administration services one of priorities. Flexible childcare and climate protections are also on his agenda.

Alshebl, who is a member of the Green Party and now has German citizenship, pledged during his campaign that once elected as mayor he would move to Ostelsheim.

  • It has been revealed that leave it up to Rachel (Jennifer Aniston), Monica (Courteney Cox), Phoebe (Lisa Kudrow), Joey (Matt LeBlanc), Chandler (Matthew Perry) and Ross (David Schwimmer) to celebrate every single season with hilarious high jinks, quotable moments and notable guest stars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We guess what we're trying to say is that we're very thankful for the Friends Thanksgiving episodes.

Though it's been 22 years since the NBC comedy came to a close, the show's holiday episodes are still one of our favorite ways to commemorate Turkey Day.

It has been revealed that leave it up to Rachel (Jennifer Aniston), Monica (Courteney Cox), Phoebe (Lisa Kudrow), Joey (Matt LeBlanc), Chandler (Matthew Perry) and Ross (David Schwimmer) to celebrate every single season with hilarious high jinks, quotable moments and notable guest stars. But there were more than laughs going around episode after episode. Sometimes, they were even educational.

Industry observers note that for instance, thanks to the ninth episode in season six, "The One Where Ross Got High," we all learned how not to make an English trifle. Sorry, Rachel, but we're sure it really did taste like feet.

And in the season five Thanksgiving episode, we learned how Chandler lost a toe.

And that's only a small taste of what Friends offered up as Thanksgiving content over its 10-season run.

Sources indicate that so the real question is, how do the episodes compare to one another? For our official ranking of the Friends Thanksgiving episodes, keep reading:.

Sources indicate that this Friends episode is at the very bottom of our own list because it's only technically a Thanksgiving episode. "The One With the List," which aired ahead of the November holiday, doesn't feature a Thanksgiving dinner, but it does have Monica making "Mocklate" treats for a newly introduced job opportunity.

The rest of the episode centers around Ross and Rachel fighting over the paleontologist making a pros and cons list to decided between Julie and Rachel.

This was the last Thanksgiving episode of the series and not its strongest. The episode centers on the gang, once again, demanding that Monica make Thanksgiving dinner, only for Ross, Phoebe, Joey and Rachel to arrive late for the meal. (Shout-out to Emma's win at the Grand Supreme Little Darling competition).

Sources indicate that what saves the episode? Ross, Joey, Rachel and Phoebe all poking their heads into Monica and Chandler's apartment to apologize. Oh, and the Bings find out they've been selected to adopt a baby.

Dogs make everything better, unless you're Chandler Bing.

According to recent reports, this season seven episode has the group's resident funnyman admitting the truth about his stance on dogs when Phoebe brings a canine friend over: He doesn't like him. "Don't do it," Joey begs Chandler as he braces himself to reveal his truth.

Chandler goes on to demand that the dog Phoebe is pet-sitting leave the apartment, but, in typical Friends fashion, the gang sneaks the pup back in. This causes a whole bunch of confusion, as a guilty Chandler goes to check on the dog, who is now supposed to be at Ross' apartment. This has him thinking that the animal is missing, which inspires Phoebe to tell a hilarious faux rescue story.

An honorable mention from the episode? Chandler's states game.

In a recent development, joey and Chandler's friendship is tested in the season four Thanksgiving episode when it's revealed that Chandler kissed Joey's girlfriend Kathy. As punishment, Joey makes his roommate spend Thanksgiving day in a box. Eventually, Joey realizes that Chandler didn't intend to hurt him but was just truly in love with Kathy, and all is forgiven. Heartwarming, right?

This episode is low on our list because we're honestly creeped out by the subplot of Monica kissing her ex Richard's son. Ugh.

Industry observers note that the gang's first Thanksgiving was an unconventional one. After leaving the apartment to see a runaway Macy's Day Parade balloon, the group returns to Monica and Rachel's apartment, only to realize they are locked out. While it's unclear whether this situation is Monica or Rachel's fault, Joey and Chandler try to help by trying every spare key they have in their apartment—which is a lot.

Sources indicate that they eventually make it inside, but dinner is ruined and Rachel has missed an notable flight. The day is saved thanks to grilled cheeses and the surprise cameo of Ugly Naked Gal, their naked neighbor's lady friend.

Industry observers note that "The One With the Football" is one of the more recognizable Friends Thanksgiving episodes, which is why it kicks off our top five. In the episode, Ross and Monica convince the group to participate in a Thanksgiving tradition from their childhood: A touch football game in which the winner receives the prized Geller Cup.

According to recent reports, as the sibling rivalry intensifies, the game becomes a battle of the sexes with the women facing off against the men. Highlights of the episode include Rachel, who had been ignored for most of the game, almost scoring the winning touchdown, Joey not knowing where Dutch people come from and Monica and Ross' bickering.

A scheduling conflict made it impossible for Reese Witherspoon to reprise her role of Jill Green for the season nine Thanksgiving episode. Instead, we met an equally unpleasant Green sister: Amy, played by the brilliant Christina Applegate.

In a recent development, in the episode, Amy is outraged that Rachel and Ross don't plan to let her raise baby Emily—reminder the child's name is actually Emma—after they die. She gets even more offended when she learns that Rachel has a huge discount at Ralph Lauren and refuses to let her use it. This sparks a hilarious hair-pulling fight, which anyone with a sister knows all too well.

Season 5, Episode 8: "The One With All the Thanksgivings".

It has been revealed that the perfect faux-flashback episode! "The One with All the Thanksgivings" helped flesh out the backstories of several characters, as it covered Monica and Chandler's first meeting—and chaotic second meeting—Joey hilariously getting a turkey stuck on his head and a peek at Phoebe's war-torn past lives.

This episode is particularly near and dear to us, as it's the first time Chandler states "I love you" to Monica.

It has been revealed that from Joey's meat sweats to a hilarious guest appearance by Brad Pitt, this one has it all. But we're getting ahead of ourselves. "The One With the Rumor" starts off with Monica declaring that she isn't going to cook a turkey since half the gang doesn't want it. Joey, unhappy about this, changes Monica's mind by promising to finish the entire bird himself.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Monica, Ross and Rachel's high school peer Will (Pitt) joins them. However, Will is upset to learn that Rachel is in attendance, as she wasn't very nice to him in high school. During the meal, Will reveals that he and Ross were in the "I Hate Rachel" club and started a rumor that she was an intersexual. (Note: This part of the plot did not age well.) Before Rachel can get fully outraged, Monica reminds her pal that she started a rumor about Ross and the 50-year-old librarian—which wasn't a rumor, per Ross' confession.

Problematic jokes aside, the dynamic between then-married Pitt and Aniston was very funny.

Things we learned from "The One Where Ross Got High," you aren't supposed to put beef in a trifle, Jacques Cousteau is dead and Chandler is a saint for putting up with the Gellers. The central theme of the episode revolves around Chandler trying to win Monica's parents' approval, because for some reason, they've never liked him.

It has been revealed that ross eventually reveals that Jack and Judy aren't fans because Ross once blamed a college pot-smoking incident on Chandler. This sets off a series of revelations, including Rachel realizing realizing that she's invented the most disgusting Thanksgiving dessert of all time. Without a doubt, "The One Where Ross Got High" has some of the most quotable lines of the series.

Every episode of Friends is streaming on HBO Max.

Newcastle United defender Sven Botman has been banned from driving.

Premier League footballer Sven Botman has been banned from driving after being caught using his mobile phone at the wheel.

The Newcastle United centre-back pleaded guilty to using a handheld mobile phone while using a motor vehicle on a road at Newcastle Magistrates' Court on Wednesday.

The 26-year-old was given six penalty points and disqualified from driving for six months, as these were added to points he had already accrued.

He was fined Â£900 and ordered to pay Â£400 costs and a Â£360 victim surcharge, the MoJ said.

Botman was driving a Land Rover on the A189 Haddricks Mill Road, in Newcastle, on 17 September when he was spotted using his phone.

The Dutchman changed his plea from not guilty to guilty at his court appearance on Wednesday, the MoJ confirmed.

Newcastle United signed Botman from Lille in 2022. He has made nine appearances so far this season, scoring one goal.

These are the animals people most want to see photographed

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, editor’s Note:  Call to Earth is a CNN editorial series committed to reporting on the environmental challenges facing our planet, together with the solutions.
  • In a recent development, originally a term used by trophy hunters in Africa, the “Major Five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo.
  • According to recent reports, however, British photographer Graeme Green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “Newly introduced Big Five” for wildlife photography.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, editor’s Note:  Call to Earth is a CNN editorial series committed to reporting on the environmental challenges facing our planet, together with the solutions. Rolex’s Perpetual Planet initiative has partnered with CNN to drive awareness and education around key sustainability concerns and to inspire positive action.

In a recent development, originally a term used by trophy hunters in Africa, the “Major Five” described the animals most challenging to shoot and kill: the lion, elephant, leopard, rhino, and buffalo. Nowadays, it is more loosely used to refer to some of Africa’s largest and most iconic animals.

According to recent reports, however, British photographer Graeme Green has reclaimed the narrative, creating a global “Newly introduced Big Five” for wildlife photography. In 2021, 50,000 people around the world voted for the five animals they would most like to photograph, or see photographed, in the wild. Five animals were crowned the winners: the elephant, polar bear, lion, gorilla and tiger.

This week, sees the publication of “The New Significant 5” photography book, which features images of those animals and other at-risk wildlife, from photography legends such as Ami Vitale, Steve McCurry and Paul Nicklen, and essays from famous conservationists and activists including like Jane Goodall and Paula Kahumbu.

Green states that the book celebrates wildlife and is a global call to action on issues impacting wildlife, including habitat loss, poaching, pollution and climate change.

Green was on assignment in Botswana at least a decade ago when he came up with the idea for a project to encourage people to “shoot with a camera, not a gun,” he indicates.

“I thought this would be a way to get people really focusing on wildlife, thinking about the wildlife they love, thinking about the animals that are at risk.”.

Ten photographs that made the world wake up to climate change.

Sources indicate that in total, the book includes the work of 144 globally renowned wildlife photographers from Ecuador to India. Curating the images took nearly two years of work, says Green.

In a recent development, “I think these are some of the most beautiful and creative images that I’ve seen put together in one book,” says Green. “These are the species that we are at risk of losing.”.

According to the UN, nature is declining at an unprecedented rate, with around one million of the planet’s animal and plant species facing extinction. The “New Significant 5,” all of which are threatened, act as ambassadors for what is happening in the natural world, notes Green.

Recent findings suggest that as well as being a powerful reminder of what we stand to lose, the book also points people towards potential solutions. Featured essays explore the benefits of rewilding and the importance of indigenous communities in conservation.

A chapter on endangered species from bees to blue whales illustrates the alarming threat climate change poses to animals outside of the “New Substantial 5.” “That’s only the tip of the iceberg – I could have included thousands of pictures because that’s how serious the situation is,” says Green.

Why a wildlife photographer took 40,000 photos to capture these extraordinary birds.

Jane Goodall, a leading conservationist who also wrote the afterword to the book, said in a press release that “we have a window of time during which we can start to heal some of the harm we have inflicted on the natural world, but only if we get together and take action now.

Sources indicate that “I hope the photos will lead people into the wonderful worlds of these iconic species. Then, perhaps, other people will become involved in helping to create a world where wildlife can flourish for future generations to enjoy,” she said.

“The Fresh Big 5: A Global Photography Project For Endangered Wildlife,” by Graeme Green, published by Earth Aware Editions, is on sale from April 4, 2023.

This story has been updated to reflect the range of complications covered by the book.

November's full moon dazzles skywatchers with a stunning Beaver Moon supermoon (photos)

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1062 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov.
  • Each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names, often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising.
  • November's full moon served as the opening salvo in a series of four dazzling supermoons, which turn full around the time that the natural satellite passes closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov. 24 and we've got the photos to prove it! Read on to see our favorite shots of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world.

Each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names, often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising. The November moon is often known as the Beaver Moon, a name associated with the time of year when beavers prepare for winter and when trappers historically set beaver traps before waterways froze.

November's full moon served as the opening salvo in a series of four dazzling supermoons, which turn full around the time that the natural satellite passes closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit.

That added proximity can make it appear noticeably brighter and larger than the smallest full moon of the year, setting the stage for an incredible photo shoot as the lunar disk climbed high into the autumn sky.

Our first shot of the moon was captured by photographer Pongmanat Tasiri as the moon rose over the roof of the Wat Phra That Doi Suthep Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, as a stunning array of craters and lunar seas scar the Beaver Moon's surface.

Meanwhile, Gary Hershorn snapped a gorgeous shot of the full yellow moon rising over the Chrysler Building in Latest York, with the Empire State Building and myriad other skyscrapers dominating the skyline.

Hershorn also managed to line up a colorful shot of the lunar disk glowing between the concrete canyon of Upcoming York's iconic 42nd Street just before moonset on the morning of Nov. 24, mere hours before the moon turned full.

NASA astronaut Anil Menon snapped a series of stunning photos from the International Space Station on Nov. 24, November full moon slipped out of view below Earth's horizon, while being gradually deformed by the warping effect of our planet's atmosphere. "Moonset today from space station - no edits to these photos from 400mm lens," Menon wrote in a post on X.

Heading back down to Earth Salih Zeki Fazlioglu took a colorful photo of the Beaver moon illuminating a thin veil of clouds above Istanbul, Turkiye, as reflected sunlight competed with the artificial glow of the city below for the viewer's attention.

According to recent reports, this shot of the lunar disk looming over the Old Post Office Pavillion in Washington D.C. was captured by David Ake, with the pink sky complementing the orange and red leaves of autumn.

Our next photo was captured by Space.com's Skywatching Editor Daisy Dobrijevic using a Sony A7IV with a Tamron 50-400mm lens as the moon shone in the skies over the city of Nottingham in the U.K. on Nov. 23.

According to recent reports, "Having seen the rather disappointing weather forecast for the night of the full moon, I decided to head out a day early and capture the almost-full Beaver Moon instead," explained Dobrijevic. "It hadn’t quite risen above the rooftops of the houses opposite me, so I took a peek down the alleyway and, sure enough, there it was, nestled between two houses, giving me just enough of a clear view to capture this close-up.".

Recent findings suggest that this striking image of the full moon rising above the Toronto skyline was snapped by Mert Alper Dervis as a flock of birds skimmed through the foreground. The outline of the lunar disk appears subtly warped and squashed by atmospheric refraction, as its reflected light passes through pockets of air with differing densities and temperatures.

Allen Berman sent in a breathtaking photo of the full moon hanging low over the Los Angeles skyline on the night of Nov. 24.

"Finding the right spot for tonight’s full moon over downtown Los Angeles was a bit tricky," Berman told Space.com. "We wound up on a neighbor’s front lawn in the Baldwin Hills section of town. The owner was a bit surprised to see photographers there. But he was cool. The conditions were perfect with thin clouds over the distant mountains that made for a magical image.".

In a recent development, moving from the modern to the old, photographer Robert Nemeti took a moody shot of the full Beaver Moon climbing skyward above the medieval Boldogkő Castle in Hungary at moonrise on Nov. 24. How many full moons must that old building have seen?

Wang Zhao snapped a very different view from Beijing, China, on that same night by using a powerful telephoto lens to capture a passenger jet as it streaked across the lunar disk, leaving dense contrails in its wake.

It has been revealed that that Beaver Moon was captured shining between the minarets of the Imam Ali Shrine in the city of Najaf, Iraq, by Karar Essa. The 53-mile-wide (85-kilometer) Tycho Crater can be seen as a distinctive bright feature below the lunar equator, close to the dark expanse of Mare Nubium.

Aris Oikonomou snapped a striking photo of the Beaver Moon shining above the Parthenon in Athens, Greece, just as night began to set in over the Acropolis.

Feeling inspired to capture your own supermoon photos? Then be sure to read our guide to photographing the moon and browse our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography because you don't have long to wait!

Industry observers note that the final supermoon of 2026 rises in just a few short weeks on Dec. 23 and it just so happens to be the closest full moon of the year, passing just 221,668 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth at the point of maximum illumination.

Sources indicate that so no excuses! We'd love to see your photo in our inbox next month.

Editor's Note: If you would like to share your full moon photos with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

#219753. Tech Report: Thuma Dupes: Japanese Joinery Bed Frames That Stack Up (2026)

📅 10 Sep 2025 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2418 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Thuma Dupes: Japanese Joinery Bed Frames That Stack Up (2026)

📅 10 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2418 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, japanese joinery bed frames are bolt-free beds made from notched wood pieces that slide and click together to make a stable frame.
  • It has been revealed that thuma is the leading brand in this space, and we love its product lineup—several members of the WIRED Reviews team have tested Thuma beds, and all rave about them.
  • It has been revealed that japanese joinery is a traditional carpentry method that uses only wooden components.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Silk & Snow (queen, with solid headboard).

In a recent development, japanese joinery bed frames are bolt-free beds made from notched wood pieces that slide and click together to make a stable frame. Think Jenga, but with really nice, sleek wooden furniture. The advantages are many, starting with easy assembly that takes just a few minutes and requires no tools.

It has been revealed that thuma is the leading brand in this space, and we love its product lineup—several members of the WIRED Reviews team have tested Thuma beds, and all rave about them. However, they’re not cheap. A Thuma bed frame starts at $895 for a twin frame with no headboard, and the king-sized Thuma signature bed our testers loved costs $2,500.

It has been revealed that japanese joinery is a traditional carpentry method that uses only wooden components. Instead of nailing boards together, each piece of wood is carved so it snugly fits into openings carved into neighboring pieces—the “joints,” if you will. The tension and strong hold of the interconnected pieces create structural integrity.

It has been revealed that it’s a pretty easy way to channel your inner Bob the Builder, and the finished bed frame looks stunning in its simplicity. However, we are always on the lookout for products at the intersection of high quality and low price—curious to see if any contenders could give Thuma a run for its money—so we researched and tested, and these are our findings.

In a recent development, be sure also to check out our guides on the best mattresses we’ve tested, as well as the best pillows and bedsheets. You’ll need something to put on your fresh frame, after all!

Updated November 2026: We’ve added two latest bed frames to this guide and ensured accuracy throughout.

DreamCloud (queen, with bamboo headboard).

I’m a longtime fan of DreamCloud mattresses, so it came as no surprise that the brand’s Japanese joinery bed frame is excellent. Like the mattress, this frame has numerous thoughtful details that stood out immediately.

DreamCloud made setup seamless. Each piece is labeled, and when it comes time to put it all together, take a gander at the endpoints of the long pieces. If you look closely at the joints where they intersect at the ends, you will see holes drilled into the top and bottom pieces. Small rods attach to the boards and fit into them, serving as a secondary mechanism to ensure stability. I find this impressive because the beams stack neatly into the grooves carved into the ends. In a word, it’s crisp. It’s a tiny detail, but the frame stayed virtually silent when I put a mattress on it or moved around in my sleep. I didn’t notice any shaking, either.

According to recent reports, another excellent feature is the frame’s center stability beam (crucial for preventing long-term sagging), which slides in last. This lets you avoid nesting it before closing the frame, unlike some other Japanese joinery models from different brands. It’s far more convenient.

In a recent development, lining up the slats is the most challenging part of the process; you have to make sure everything is aligned perfectly. To help the process go smoothly, you’ll find wooden rods—similar to those on the ends of the boards—in the center of the bed, where you insert the slatted frames. They’re about the width of a pencil. Pop those slats in, unroll, Velcro to keep in place, and go.

You don’t need a headboard with this frame, but DreamCloud provided one for testing. Two square openings are located inside the top beam of the frame, right where your head would be. The headboard slides into these internal slots, which hold the end pieces and keep it upright. Foam block stickers are included to be attached last, so your wall doesn’t get scuffed up. All that, and still no tools necessary. Down to the details, people! And this detail you don’t want to skip—it’s around $449 for a queen. The headboard costs $299 extra, but even with that, it’s still far cheaper than luxury alternatives. You’ll also have two stain options: natural or a very pretty walnut.

In a recent development, that said, you’ll have to consider how many sleepers will use this frame and the weight of the mattress you’ll place on it. When I was testing newly introduced mattresses every week, two of the frame’s center support legs split right down the middle. Make sure you don’t screw them on too tightly, as I suspect the tension is what made the wood look like I had been chopping it with a small axe. Regardless, I was shocked to see this happen, and it is another notch on Thuma’s belt for heightened durability. —Julia Forbes.

The Bamboo Bed Frame by DreamCloud ranges from $299 for a twin to $549 for a California king (frame only).

Silk & Snow (queen, with solid headboard).

Silk & Snow is another brand that I hold in high regard. Every time I’ve tested a mattress from the brand, it consistently packs quality for the price. This platform bed frame was no exception. There are two options: natural rubberwood and acacia wood. I opted for the latter, which is a medium-brown color. I thought that the stain was stunning, with a richness akin to a lovely latte. However, I really appreciate that they offer options not just in wood stain color, but also in the actual hardwood itself.

Recent findings suggest that this frame arrived in four separate boxes. I liked this approach because it protected the wood stain’s integrity during shipping. Every other frame in this guide was packed into one box—not unlike a mattress-in-a-box, but heavier and longer. I actually preferred this route, as every box was also labeled for easy setup.

Like the DreamCloud frame, Silk & Snow’s doesn’t require tools or hardware to set up—it’s made entirely of wood. One thing I learned the hard way: Make sure the center beam is within the frame perimeter before fully closing it off. Then place the slats into the internal notches on the side rails, and it’s ready for a mattress. I had no issues with noise, shaking, or feeling unstable. It supported a mattress just fine, and I am still truly enamored with how the wood stain looked amidst my studio’s decor.

Recent findings suggest that however, I do a lot of testing, so I’m constantly setting up and taking down mattresses, frames, and bedding. This is where having two people will be crucial, as I decided to do it all by myself for the sake of time, to the detriment of the frame. The frame got badly scratched up around the slatted portions where the corners of the boards stack together, due to my awkward solo assembly motions. I doubt you’ll be doing this as much as I do, but it was still a bit disappointing to see. Despite this, it’s worth recommending because I loved how it looked and performed. —Julia Forbes.

The Silk & Snow Wooden Platform bed frame ranges from $550 for a twin to $900 for a king (frame only).

Sources indicate that the Avocado City Bed Frame is a minimalist wood (blonde or walnut) platform frame with a completely tool-free Japanese-joinery assembly process. The same natural, nontoxic, and sustainable materials practices that guide the company’s mattresses are at play here as well.

Recent findings suggest that the City Bed is regularly $1,299 for a queen, and it is the most affordable of Avocado’s bed options (though you have to factor in a shipping fee). It’s made from very nice, solid wood (I tested the walnut version). There’s an optional headboard that I did not test. The bed itself is attractive, fairly subtle, and unobtrusive. In fact, if your duvet is reasonably large, you may not even see much of the bedframe.

In a recent development, the frame fits together using interlocking joints with metal reinforcements. In my testing, it’s been solid and sturdy, with no squeaking or any signs of weak joints. It is a tight fit at times, especially at the four corners, and I had to tap it with a soft mallet to get it fully flush (which sort of defeats the no-tool promise, but you probably could have done the same with a copy of Infinite Jest or something equally solid). —Scott Gilbertson.

The Avocado City bed frame ranges from $750 for a twin to $1,499 for a California king (frame only).

The Birch frame was the most basic of the Thuma dupes I tested. I was really excited about this one because the wood is sourced from the land of the pines, otherwise known as my home state of North Carolina. Poplar is a durable hardwood, and southern yellow pine is one of the harder pine woods. (I can attest to this because, for an eighth-grade science project, I tested the durability of regional woods.) The manufacturing partner is a certified member of the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC). The legs are made of a completely different wood, Appalachian maple. It also uses a soy-based resin to remain completely formaldehyde-free.

It arrived in two boxes, and setup was quick and easy—the step-by-step instructions were the most thorough of the bunch. With written descriptions and pictures, it’s hard to mess this up. Plus, you don’t need any tools to get this frame up and running. The outer boards were polished to maintain the gorgeous hue of the pine wood. However, be cautious when handling the inner slatted-board sections, as this wood is not finished. I got a small splinter and was not a happy camper. Next, I set up the bed and slept on it for a week—the standard amount of time I test mattresses. The first few days, this thing creaked and moaned like crazy. It didn’t feel stable, and I was shaken if I moved even slightly. By the end of the week, it seemed to fall into place and settle, so I no longer noticed the noise or motion.

Recent findings suggest that I don’t want to discount this as a possible option, though, because the wood quality was what I wanted it to be, and so was the overall price. If you’re looking for a cheaper option for a guest room, upgrading your teen’s room, or furnishing a first apartment on a budget, this could work well for you. —Julia Forbes.

The Birch Madison bed frame ranges from $749 for a twin to $978 for a California king.

Nectar Sleep (queen, frame only).

Nectar Sleep (queen, with bamboo headboard).

Recent findings suggest that I had never set up or slept on a Japanese joinery-style bed frame before testing this model from Nectar, and now I’m a true believer. The frame is made from bamboo, and assembly took just about 20 minutes with no tools required.

Putting it together was super simple: the four feet had cut-out notches where the frame slid into place, and you just needed to push down to make the pieces lock together—it’s essentially like putting together a giant set of Lincoln Logs. After sliding the footboard into the feet’s notches, you finish both sides the same way by pushing down into the notches. The middle section is springy and has a floating foot to adjust for the bed’s pressure, so no cumbersome box spring is needed. The slats are connected with Velcro and just need to be unspooled and adhered to the sides. I opted for a headboard that slides in from above and stays in place because of the cutouts on the head portion of the frame below.

I’m physically disabled, so putting together furniture with tools and nails or screws is nearly impossible. I recommend that anyone who’s in a similar position check out a Japanese-style bed frame, as it’s lightweight, requires no additional tools, and requires very little physical strength. Plus, this frame comes in two colors, has optional headboard attachments, a 60-night home trial, a two-year warranty, and free shipping. —Molly Higgins.

The Nectar Bamboo bed frame ranges from $299 for a twin to $549 for a California king (frame only).

Industry observers note that here’s the thing: Thuma is still a Japanese joinery bed frame. Therefore, I’d be remiss not to include it on this list. While I can vouch that the options above are credible dupes, many of my teammates feel nothing beats the original in this case.

Recent findings suggest that thuma’s Classic Bed Frame is made from upcycled, sturdy rubberwood that comes in four finishes: walnut, natural, espresso, and gray. You can also choose different headboard variations, including all-wood, a pillow board (Italian wool and foam), or a hybrid of the two. The design’s not only beautiful, but it’s also backed by certifications such as UL GreenGuard Gold and CertiPur-US (if you opt for the pillow board).

It has been revealed that WIRED Gear Editor Julian Chokkattu has had his Thuma frame for several years, and he notes it takes next to no time to set up. He also loves that it doesn’t creak or slide—just a strong sense of security while sleeping on it.

The Thuma Classic bed frame ranges from $895 for a twin to $1,495 for a California king (frame only).

Just like with the best mattresses we regularly test, each frame required a week of testing (not including naps) to evaluate night-over-night performance. This also allowed time for the frames to settle into place and perform alongside the bed each was paired with.

How Do I Set Up a Japanese Joinery Bed Frame?

Your bed frame should come with installation instructions, whether it features Japanese joinery construction or not. In the same vein, I recommend having someone assist you with the setup. As mentioned in our Silk & Snow review, this helps mitigate the risk of bumping and scratching your upcoming furniture.

Are These Bed Frames Better Than Thuma’s?

We wouldn’t say better, just different. Each brand offers its own approach to creating a bed frame that adheres to the Japanese joinery method. This could include the type of wood used, the stains offered, the types of headboards you can pair it with, where it was manufactured, and, of course, the price.

Latest Update: Iordanescu ready for Watford 'challenge'

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Edward Iordandescu is the first Romanian to manage in the top four tiers of English football.
  • Latest Watford boss Edward Iordanescu says he has inherited a "challenge" but also "an opportunity" as the club seeks to pull away from the Championship relegation zone.
  • The 48-year-old has replaced Alessio Dionisi, who was sacked on Sunday after only five months in charge, following a run of seven defeats in 10 league games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Edward Iordandescu is the first Romanian to manage in the top four tiers of English football.

Latest Watford boss Edward Iordanescu says he has inherited a "challenge" but also "an opportunity" as the club seeks to pull away from the Championship relegation zone.

The 48-year-old has replaced Alessio Dionisi, who was sacked on Sunday after only five months in charge, following a run of seven defeats in 10 league games.

Iordanescu became Watford's sixth upcoming boss in less than 18 months and is the 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

He will take charge of the Hornets for the first time on Saturday when they travel to bottom club Derby County.

The Romanian met the media for the first time on Friday, and set out his vision for his tenure.

The Watford job is Iordanescu's first since leaving Legia Warsaw in October 2025, having won the Polish Super Cup with them last season.

It is the 10th managerial post of his 15-year coaching career, which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj - who he guided to the Romanian title and two domestic cups after joining midway through the 2020-21 season.

He also spent two and a half years in charge of Romania, guiding them to the last 16 of Euro 2024, where they were beaten by the Netherlands.

However, in his first job in English football, he inherits a Watford side three points above the drop zone and facing a fight for their second-tier status.

"I'm proud more than anything else and I'm honoured and happy to be here, but I'm also very aware of the challenge in front of me," Iordanescu told BBC Three Counties Radio.

It has been revealed that "I don't want to make promises. I know the fans are not happy in this moment, but also I know that my words are not enough to bring them back, so they wait for facts. We need that, but of course there is a lot of work to do, there is a process in front of us and I hope we make the next steps right away.

Sources indicate that "For me it's a challenge but at the same time it's an opportunity and I want to transform this opportunity into something good for the club, for the fans. This is the most important [thing].".

Prior to the dismissal of Dionisi, former Watford player Tom Ince - who left the club at the end of the 2025-26 season - told the BBC's 72+ Podcast there was "so much control away from the manager" at Vicarage Road.

While Ince, now at League Two side Tranmere Rovers, added his respect of positives of chairman Gino Pozzo's practises, he is not alone in speaking out about the board's influence.

Former England boss Sam Allardyce stated he turned down the Watford job in 2019 after claiming he was told how the side should play and which players should be in the XI.

But Iordandescu revealed that is not his expectation.

"I know my borders and I know my responsibilities." he said. "I'm in this club with a lot of quality people, professionals, people that know, understand, in detail, football, but starting yesterday I'm the number one in the technical side.

"I don't believe there's somebody here in the club that can overcome the coach, taking the technical knowledge, so it will be my responsibility, but also the technical part will be my decision all the time.".

Pioneer or coach-eater? The complex world of Pozzo's Watford.

From a purely statistical perspective, Watford's laboured start to the season under Dionisi could be credited to one key deficiency.

The Hornets have scored the fewest goals in the Championship, with only 13 in their 17 matches so far.

However, Iordanescu said his primary objective was not to thrill, but to win.

He said: "I always prefer to win 1-0 than 4-2. One-nil means you have an organised team, a team with some responsibility to engage 100% and to give everything for the result.

"So for me the priority is not to score more goals - [it is] to start to be organised, to start to act and react together on the pitch, to start to understand that the mindset should be a little bit different than what it was until now and to start to be efficient.

"In time we will see about scoring more goals, definitely every coach wants the team to score as much as possible.".

Edward Iordanescu: My blueprint for Watford.

Iordanescu also appeared to confirm he was in talks about taking over while Dionisi was still in charge.

It was reported on 12 November that the Hertfordshire club were in talks with him, but Dionisi, who had only been appointed in June, remained in charge across the international break and for Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United.

The Italian was sacked on Sunday, with Iordanescu appointed on Wednesday.

Iordanescu said he had "asked for time" from the Watford hierachy before accepting the role.

He stated: "I wanted to understand very clearly the objectives, the targets, so when I gave the final response, I was aware of everything.

"I'm here, I'm enthusiastic, I'm positive, I'm confident we can do good things together, and the thing which I count most on is the potential of this very young team. One of the youngest teams in the league.".

But Iordanescu also took time to pay tribute to his predecessor.

"He [Dionisi] definitely worked hard," said Iordanescu.

"He did and left good things, very good things, already I saw many of them. But in football when things don't run the way you want and when the results are not backing up your work, it's difficult.

"I know he is a coach that put a lot of heart in his work and thank him for the good things that he did, and also tried to achieve here.".

The task at hand now for Iordanescu is to succeed where Dionisi, and so many other Hornets bosses since their Premier League relegation in 2022, could not.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lowe's on Wednesday posted strong quarterly results and raised its full-year outlook as the firm said it saw strength among professional shoppers.

Sources indicate that the firm mentioned comparable sales grew 1.8% for the fiscal third quarter, driven by a 17.4% increase in online sales and "solid" performance in pro and home services sales. Net sales rose to $22.76 billion.

In a recent development, because of the strength, Lowe's now mentioned it expects full-year sales of roughly $92.5 billion, up from a previous projection of $92 billion. It also expects comparable sales to be up 0.5%, compared with previous guidance of flat.

CEO Marvin Ellison told CNBC that the organization is focused on growing despite economic headwinds and a sluggish housing market. He remarked Lowe's posted its sixth straight quarterly comparable sales increase and saw particular strength in appliances, which saw its largest revenue growth in five years.

"We believe irrespective of the macro environment we're in, we're going to take share because there's a lot of share out there that we can go and get, and we're going to be aggressive to go and get that share," Ellison told CNBC.

According to recent reports, lowe's also reported a pretax benefit of approximately $250 million from tariff refunds during the quarter, which contributed a 34-cent boost to earnings per share. Ellison said the organization aims to use those funds to enhance the customer experience and bring value to shoppers.

He added that do-it-yourself customers and pro shoppers are not investing in major renovation projects but are instead spending on repair and maintenance projects.

Sources indicate that "We are giving those pros what they need," he said. "We're able to improve our fulfillment capabilities and our pro loyalty program.".

Here's how the firm performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

It has been revealed that for the quarter ended Oct. 30, Lowe's reported net income of $1.67 billion, or $2.98 per share, compared with $1.62 billion, or $2.88 per share, the year prior.

The home improvement retailer has previously noted it's seeing "pressure" on spending on projects, especially as consumers are stretched thin by inflation and macroeconomic uncertainty. The company is also battling a slower housing market and higher mortgage rates.

Ellison previously told CNBC he expects consumers to remain cautious through the end of the year.

Lowe's executives stated on a call with analysts Wednesday that the tech giant is continuing to battle high fuel costs, which they said accelerated through the third quarter. CFO Brandon Sink said diesel prices are right now around $6 per gallon, up about 15% overall compared to what the company saw in the second quarter.

"So we're trying to continue to manage that, balance that, and we're reflecting that into our Q4 guide," Sink mentioned.

Ellison told CNBC the company remains optimistic about consumer spending this holiday season and that November sales are in line with expectations so far.

Lowe's competitor Home Depot mentioned earlier this week that it's seeing resilience among professional shoppers and reported comparable sales growth.

Astronomers discover the most distant and ancient supermassive black hole-powered quasar in the universe

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (636 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun.
  • The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Major Bang.
  • The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun.

The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Major Bang. 40 million years further back in time than the previous record holder for the most ancient quasar.

The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe. That's because previously, scientists had theorized it should take 1 billion years of feeding and merging for black holes to reach supermassive status of millions or billions of times as massive as the sun.

Quasars occur when supermassive black holes are surrounded by vast amounts of gas and dust on which they feed. The immense gravitational influence of the black hole causes this material, in the form of an accretion disk, to glow brightly and to blast out bright jets of plasma. That means quasars at the heart of galaxies in regions called active galactic nuclei (AGNs) like this one can often be brighter than the combined light of every star in the entire surrounding galaxy, but only briefly.

The newly discovered quasar, designated J1504+6252 and nicknamed Dún Aonghasa, is in this brief phase of its existence. It was discovered among millions of objects in 18 months of data from Euclid.

In a recent development, euclid's initial observation of Dún Aonghasa was followed up by an array of ground-based and space-based telescopes, including the W.M. Keck Observatory, the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory, the Hubble Space Telescope, and ultimately the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). It was the JWST that determined the mass of this supermassive black hole.

What is interesting about Dún Aonghasa is that it is unlike other supermassive black holes seen at a similar period of the early universe. That's because this black hole is feeding relatively slowly. That means if it engaged in rapid feeding to reach its massive size, that period of gorging on gas and dust has either ended or it has paused.

That is something that further complicates our picture of supermassive black hole growth.

By staring back 13.1 billion years in time to see Dún Aonghasa, Euclid is also observing a crucial time in cosmic history when the first stars and galaxies were taking shape, and the clearing of cosmic gas was ending the dark ages of our universe by allowing light to travel freely.

Euclid's primary mission is improving our understanding of dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the expansion of the universe, and dark matter, the most mysterious "stuff" in the cosmos. Collectively, these aspects of the universe account for around 95% of its matter-energy budget and have come to be collectively referred to as the dark universe. Hence Euclid's nickname as the "dark universe detective.".

This research, along with Euclid's discovery of at least 12 that date back around 13 billion years, shows that this pioneering space telescope launched in 2023 could also make a major contribution to our understanding of black holes and their growth.

According to recent reports, the team's research was published on Tuesday (Nov. 24) in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

He also writes about science communication for Elsevier and the European Journal of Physics. Rob holds a bachelor of science degree in physics and astronomy from the U.K.’s Open University. Ryan Naderi has netted some crucial goals for Derek McInnes this term.

Derek McInnes claims Rangers should not experience any anxiety about the prospect of going top of the Scottish Premiership as the Ibrox side look to extend their four-match winning run.

Rangers host in-form Falkirk on Saturday (15:00 GMT), who have won six on the bounce in the league, and victory would move McInnes' team top before leaders Celtic travel to face Hearts on Sunday.

"I don't think there should be anxiety when you're trying to go top of the league at all," McInnes said.

"Obviously, you want to be top of the league come the end of the season.

"If you've got an opportunity to go there, it's notable you try and take it.".

Ryan Naderi netted an early second-half equaliser then set up Djeidi Gassama as Rangers turned a 1-0 deficit into a 3-1 lead before Aberdeen scored a consolation in Tuesday's Premiership match at Ibrox.

It was Naderi's 11th goal of the season and McInnes spoke of his awareness of the now Czech Republic international last season while managing Hearts, who have used a data analytics firm for much of their recent recruitment.

"Last January, obviously, when we first saw that Rangers were linked with Naderi, like everything else, I would say to [Hearts sporting director] Graeme Jones, 'how do they rate him?'.

"Because you're always curious, it's just the way it is. It's brilliant when you see other teams round about you signing a player that's not rated!

Industry observers note that "He was someone that I think was well known to them. Brugge had an interest in Ryan, I think, and I think USG potentially had an interest in him as well but the kind of money, the fee, it just went away from them.

"The feeling was that he could help Rangers and make them better.

"I had a good conversation with Ryan when I first came in the door and what we felt this season could look like for him.

"He's stood up brilliantly to the injuries to Youssef [Chermiti] and Lawrence [Shankland] and he's had to be the guy. He's led the line brilliantly and I love the goals he scores. All top strikers have intelligence to be in the right place at the right time.".

"The club's well aware of what needs to be done and what we shouldn't be doing and Ryan's been part of that conversation.".

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera spacecraft has captured its first close-up image of the Didymos asteroid system, offering scientists a surprising upcoming perspective on the site of NASA's historic asteroid deflection experiment.
  • On September 26, 2022, NASA's DART spacecraft deliberately crashed into Dimorphos, the smaller of the two asteroids in the system.
  • Sources indicate that the image was taken from a distance of 60 km using Hera's monochromatic Asteroid Framing Camera, which captures images in black and white.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Space Agency's (ESA) Hera spacecraft has captured its first close-up image of the Didymos asteroid system, offering scientists a surprising upcoming perspective on the site of NASA's historic asteroid deflection experiment.

On September 26, 2022, NASA's DART spacecraft deliberately crashed into Dimorphos, the smaller of the two asteroids in the system. Hera's latest image provides a look at its larger companion, Didymos, from a side that scientists had not previously seen in such detail.

Sources indicate that the image was taken from a distance of 60 km using Hera's monochromatic Asteroid Framing Camera, which captures images in black and white. Although most of Dimorphos, which measures 151 m across, is concealed in shadow, the much larger Didymos, with a diameter of 780 m, is clearly visible.

A Surprisingly Different Side of Asteroid Didymos.

"The first thing we said was wow!" observes Hera Principal Investigator Patrick Michel, Director of Research at CNRS / Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur. "This is the other side of Didymos from the one that DART's camera showed us shortly before impact, so this feels like looking at a whole upcoming world.

"This side of Didymos has the same central ridge along its equator that we saw before, but otherwise appears very different, with multiple boulders and craters and what look like patterns of grooves or ridges.".

The newly revealed terrain raises intriguing questions about how the asteroid's surface developed and whether NASA's collision with Dimorphos may have left traces on its larger neighbor.

When DART struck Dimorphos, the impact sent material flying into space. Scientists believe some of that debris may have traveled across the roughly 1 km separating the two asteroids and reached Didymos. Determining whether this material contributed to the features now visible on its surface will be an crucial part of Hera's investigation.

ESA's Hera mission scientist Michael Kueppers adds: "Since we expect a lot of impact-ejected material to have made it across the approximately 1 km of space from Dimorphos to Didymos, it may be that some of these characteristics originate from this transport of material, and we have exciting work ahead of us to sort it out. We look forward to seeing much more of both bodies and systemically mapping all the changes we identify.".

NASA's DART Mission Changed an Asteroid's Orbit.

Although Dimorphos is largely obscured in Hera's new image, it holds a remarkable place in space exploration history. It became the first object in the Solar System to have its orbit measurably altered by human activity.

NASA achieved this milestone by sending the 580 kg DART spacecraft into Dimorphos at approximately 6.1 km/s. The collision reduced the time the smaller asteroid takes to complete an orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, give or take a minute. That change was substantially greater than scientists had anticipated.

The experiment demonstrated that striking an asteroid with a spacecraft can change its motion through space. This approach, known as kinetic impact deflection, could potentially be used to redirect a dangerous asteroid before it reaches Earth.

Hera Begins Its Investigation of NASA's Asteroid Impact.

After a two-year journey, Hera has reached the double asteroid system, located 196.8 million km from Earth. The spacecraft is now preparing for a detailed 'crash site investigation' to examine the consequences of NASA's groundbreaking experiment.

While DART demonstrated that an asteroid's orbit could be changed through a deliberate collision, Hera will help scientists understand the physical processes behind the result. By examining both asteroids and documenting their characteristics, researchers hope to improve their ability to predict how future asteroid deflection attempts might work.

Industry observers note that the findings could help transform kinetic impact deflection from a successful one-time demonstration into a dependable, repeatable planetary defense technique. Such a capability could prove critical if an asteroid were ever discovered on a collision course with Earth.

Industry observers note that "Seeing this image is a hugely exciting moment for the whole Hera family," comments Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli. "It has taken years of hard work and dedication to reach this point - but we're motivated to know that the adventure is only beginning!".

The mission's next major reveal is scheduled for November 25, when detailed images of both Didymos and Dimorphos will be unveiled, giving scientists and the public a closer look at the asteroids involved in humanity's first successful asteroid deflection experiment.

Materials provided by European Space Agency (ESA). Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Africa is a land of opportunity." "The German-African relationship is a win-win." "The continent is the market of the future.".
  • That's what many business leaders and politicians have to say about Africa at the sixth edition of the German-African Business Summit in Accra, Ghana.
  • German firms are increasingly viewing Africa as an attractive destination as they scramble to find new markets amid wars in Ukraine and Iran, high energy prices, punishing US tariffs and slowing growth in traditional markets like China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Africa is a land of opportunity." "The German-African relationship is a win-win." "The continent is the market of the future.".

That's what many business leaders and politicians have to say about Africa at the sixth edition of the German-African Business Summit in Accra, Ghana. While these descriptions aren't new, there's a palpable sense of urgency and seriousness this time.

German firms are increasingly viewing Africa as an attractive destination as they scramble to find new markets amid wars in Ukraine and Iran, high energy prices, punishing US tariffs and slowing growth in traditional markets like China.

"For a long time, many German companies had a secure source of revenue from the major export markets in North America and China, but the geopolitical ruptures of our time have undermined this certainty," German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier stated during the event.

"One could also say that it is time for new horizons, time to take a closer look at economic opportunities still waiting for us.".

It has been revealed that africa is home to some of the fastest growing economies in the world, like Ethiopia and Rwanda. Even as European and other advanced economies contend with declining working-age populations, Africa is expected to add hundreds of millions of workers in the next few decades, emerging as a key source of future labor.

Germany has already signed a migration pact with Kenya and is working on one with Ghana as it seeks to attract skilled workers to help ease acute labor shortages in certain sectors at home.

Even as Africa remains one of the poorest regions in the world, economic growth in parts of the continent has created a larger and more affluent consumer class over the past three decades. This group is aspirational and a growing source of demand for many of the goods that German firms want to sell, from cars to cosmetics.

The continent, with its mineral wealth and renewable energy potential, is central to European Union efforts to diversify its sources of critical raw materials and reduce reliance on China-dominated supply chains.

It is also playing an increasingly key role in strengthening the EU's energy security after the bloc phased out most energy imports from Russia.

German firms have committed to invest billions of euros in green hydrogen projects in countries such as Mauritania and Namibia.

"We don't have the capital to develop them [natural resources]. So foreign investors are coming to help us develop those resources. Whilst we are getting jobs and industrialization is taking place, they are also making profits," said Amin Amidu Sulemani, energy and infrastructure commissioner at the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

"It's not a relationship where we send raw materials outside of Africa every time, when we can actually process them here," he told DW.

Despite Africa's growing economic appeal, many obstacles to investment remain, including corruption and governance concerns, unreliable energy supplies, foreign exchange risk and poor infrastructure.

African leaders say they are working to address these challenges and improve the ease of doing business.

Yet while German companies have largely remained on the sidelines, competitors from countries such as the UAE, Turkey and India have made significant inroads across the continent.

German firms enjoy a strong reputation in Africa because of their engineering expertise, vocational training programs and long-term industrial investments, which are more likely to create stable jobs than investments in extractive industries.

However, they have struggled to translate that goodwill into a larger commercial presence. Africa, for instance, accounts for less than 2% of the total foreign investment made by German firms over the past several decades.

It has been revealed that business leaders complain that German firms lack adequate financing and risk protection for projects in Africa. They also criticize excessive bureaucracy and the absence of a coherent German strategy, with engagement fragmented across ministries and agencies.

Industry bodies say German institutions and firms often perceive risks too broadly, treating diverse African markets as if they pose the same level of risk.

In a recent development, "German companies can be a bit more bold and maybe also innovative in the way they approach the continent," Khadi Camara, deputy CEO of the German-African Business Association, told DW. "We see that in the companies that are successful, they don't do business as usual. Every country has its nuances that companies keep in mind and say, okay, this model works here, that model works there.".

The 2026 World Investment Report by UN trade body UNCTAD revealed that investors from the Gulf and Asia are becoming notable sources of investment in Africa, especially in energy, logistics, real estate and infrastructure.

The UAE has been a major investor in greenfield megaprojects in recent years, including the $34 billion (€31 billion) Infinity Power renewable energy project in Mauritania, the $24 billion Ras El Hikma real estate development project in Egypt and the $6 billion H2 Global Energy hydrogen project in Tunisia.

Business leaders are calling for better financing and guarantees, and more risk-sharing and fewer bureaucratic hurdles.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, others, including the German president, are urging German businesses to take on more risk and seize opportunities in Africa. Otherwise, they risk being edged out by foreign rivals.

"Be curious, take risks and invest in our common future," Steinmeier mentioned.
